scope: Requirements coverage and focused improvements to existing learning and authoring workflows. Existing sprint 1-5 GitHub states were verified closed before work began.

requirements.findings: GitHub issues 1-22 and five local sprint plans already existed. Sprint 6 adds tracked enhancement issues 23-24.

React/TypeScript frontend, Node/Express/TypeScript backend, MongoDB persistence, username/email login, registration, mandatory consent and student/faculty roles. Administrators, editable profiles and avatars were added in prior commits.

Subjects have name, unique normalized code, term and year level. Faculty-owned subject/module creation and a public catalog already exist. Catalog had no personalized progress or assessment coverage overview.
requirements.improvement: Add verified student mastery, course status, next-lesson actions and faculty-owned assessment readiness to the catalog.

requirements.findings: Ordered modules provide summaries, Markdown lecture text and authenticated file/presentation downloads. Progression requires a recorded completion and a passing submission on the designated assessment. Opening a course previously selected the first unlocked lesson even when it was already mastered.
requirements.improvement: Use the shared verified completion rules in a batched overview and open the first unfinished lesson. Faculty can locate the first module missing assessment coverage.

requirements.findings: Manual authoring, JSON/CSV/Aiken bank imports and lecture text/file extraction already feed a reviewed question bank. Server-controlled attempts save drafts, shuffle questions/options, grade and persist results, and unlock prerequisite progression. Earlier committed settings allow faculty-set passing marks (default 75%) and per-question timing; this intentionally exceeds the original fixed 75% and 10-20 minute wording and is retained.

Student-only result summaries and faculty-owned gradebooks include surname/score/date sorting, search, year/section/subject/status/score filters, mandatory separate cohort tables, and PDF/Excel exports. Reports count all matching attempts, including retakes. This sprint preserves those semantics.

A public searchable lesson directory already exposes metadata, summaries and syllabuses, with full lesson content protected by authenticated prerequisite checks. The public subject catalog remains available without personalized progress.

selectedSprint.name: Course Progress and Assessment Readiness
selectedSprint.reason: Make earned progress and missing assessment coverage visible at course selection, while improving catalog error recovery and keyboard access.
selectedSprint.databaseMigration: None. Overview is derived from existing subjects, modules, quizzes, progress and submissions.

analysisMethod.sources: Requirements, README, sprint plans, direct source review, GitHub issue states, service graph, backend integration tests and browser workflows.
analysisMethod.graphScope: backend/src/services only: 9 files, 40 nodes, 56 edges; structural extraction used zero LLM tokens.
analysisMethod.graphLimitation: The scoped extraction reported 36 dangling edges to symbols outside the service corpus. It is incomplete for cross-layer relationships; controllers, models, routes and frontend flows were inspected directly instead of inferring those connections.

verificationLimits: Automated checks use isolated local MongoDB, not a live MongoDB Atlas deployment.
Readiness indicates valid quiz linkage, not pedagogical review or publication approval.
Course progress reflects the current designated quiz and existing recorded completion evidence; it is not an enrollment roster.
